Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Expectation2: Coordinate with other air traffic controllers to ensure smooth traffic flow
Situation2: Thunderstorm cells force multiple flights to reroute, increasing handoffs between sectors.
Story: My headset crackled with urgent voices as I scanned the radar, tracking a dozen blips weaving through the storm. The thunderstorm had thrown the whole sector into chaos, and every controller was stretched thin. My supervisor’s voice echoed in my mind: “Stay sharp, coordinate every handoff, no mistakes.” Just then, my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his voice tight with panic. “I think I left my passport at home. My flight’s in two hours. Can you check and bring it to the airport? Please, I can’t miss this.” I glanced at the clock, heart pounding. Sam had always been there for me, and I knew he was counting on me now. But the radar screen was alive with shifting storms and blinking alerts, every second demanding my full attention. My team needed me focused, but Sam needed me too. I stared at the phone, torn between the chaos in the sky and the desperation in my friend’s voice, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in, waiting for me to choose.
